extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, patent draftspersons, and USPTO examiners preparing or reviewing U.S. patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for preparing, formatting, submitting, correcting, and publishing drawings in U.S. patent (utility, design, plant, and statutory invention registration) applications, including processing/office procedures and applicable CFR/USC rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required where necessary (35 U.S.C. 113 / 37 CFR 1.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented. Whenever the nature of the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and the applicant has not furnished such a drawing, the examiner will require its submission within a time period of not less than two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must be filed with the application (or required within at least two months). Retain originals for future correction. See 35 U.S.C. 113 and 37 CFR 1.81(a),(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings cannot be used to cure insufficiency or supplement original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted after the filing date of the application may not be used (i) to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of an enabling disclosure or otherwise inadequate disclosure therein, or (ii) to supplement the original disclosure thereof for the purpose of interpretation of the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on late drawings to fix specification defects or to broaden/clarify original claims' scope. See 35 U.S.C. 113 and 37 CFR 1.81(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must reference drawings (37 CFR 1.74)
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are drawings, there shall be a brief description of the several views of the drawings and the detailed description of the invention shall refer to the different views by specifying the numbers of the figures and to the different parts by use of reference letters or numerals (preferably the latter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief description should identify each drawing; if subdivided views (e.g., FIG. 6A, 6B) the brief description may state FIG. 6 only unless specific subfigures are named. Ensure consistency between drawings and specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every claimed feature (37 CFR 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Conventional features not essential for understanding may be shown as graphical symbols or labeled representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invention is improvement on old machine, show improved portion disconnected and also show sufficient old structure to show connection (37 CFR 1.83(b)). Examiner may require additional illustration within at least two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black ink drawings standard (37 CFR 1.84(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required. India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer-generated 'black ink' drawings are acceptable if substantially equivalent in quality to manual drafting; minimize jagged/wavy lines. Artwork should be professional quality. Computer screen images may be acceptable when necessary for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings permitted only in limited circumstances (37 CFR 1.84(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings may be necessary as the only practical medium to disclose the subject matter; they are accepted only after granting a petition and meeting specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include fee, three sets of color drawings, a black-and-white photocopy (historically required but waiver noted in comments), and an amendment to the brief description noting color drawings. Color drawings must be reproducible in black-and-white for publication; special distribution rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs only when practicable (37 CFR 1.84(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photomicrographs, are not ordinarily permitted but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (examples include gels, blots, histological sections, animals, plants, crystalline structures, ornamental effects for design patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Photographs cannot be removed from applications; keep originals. Mounted photographs are objectionable; glossy paper for photos is permitted. Color photos follow color-drawing conditions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms as drawings (37 CFR 1.84(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings. Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure; each group of waveforms must be a single figure with a common vertical axis and time along the horizontal axis; each waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification may contain chemical formulas and equations (37 CFR 1.58) but flowcharts, waveforms, graphs must be submitted as drawings. Sequence listings and program listings have special rules (comments refer to 37 CFR 1.96 and sequence rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of paper (37 CFR 1.84(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable. All sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds. Only one side of the sheet may be used. Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size and margin requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not object if photographs are on shiny/glossy paper (waiver). Avoid folding; transmit by mail with binder's board protection where possible. Mounted photographs are objectionable as of enforcement date noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of paper (37 CFR 1.84(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size. Acceptable sizes are 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8½ by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT/national stage specifics: international record copy must be A4; national stage U.S. copies may be A4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight area (37 CFR 1.84(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames, should have scan target points printed on two cater-corner margin corners. Each sheet must include top margin ≥2.5 cm (1 inch), left margin ≥2.5 cm, right margin ≥1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom margin ≥1.0 cm (3/8 inch), leaving a sight no greater than specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow exact margin figures to ensure reproducible sight area; include scan cross-hairs. See guide for precise sight dimensions for each sheet size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — exploded, partial, sectional, alternate position, modified forms (37 CFR 1.84(h) & subparas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Views must follow the subparagraph rules: exploded views (h)(1), partial views (h)(2), sectional views including hatching (h)(3), alternate position (h)(4), and modified forms (h)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate proper use (e.g., exploded views may use brackets; sectional views require hatching/shading techniques; partial views should be labeled separately). See examples in Appendix 4 for each view type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views (37 CFR 1.84(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Views should be arranged on the sheet so that words appear in a horizontal, left-to-right fashion when the page is either upright or turned so that the top becomes the right side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure orientation/readability; examples show acceptable arrangements. Words should be horizontal in the allowed page orientations described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view requirements (37 CFR 1.84(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: A view including the overall organization of the device suitable for publication on the front page of the patent application publication and the front page of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an overall informative view for the front page; ensure it meets character of lines, numbering, and other drawing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale (37 CFR 1.84(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale must be used and indicated appropriately where necessary so that the drawings accurately represent the invention and details are clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scale is used, indicate the scale on the figure; ensure scale choices do not obscure details. (Guide references a Scale paragraph in 37 CFR 1.84; follow office examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters (37 CFR 1.84(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines, numbers, and letters must have proper character: continuous thick lines for edging/outlining, consistent lettering and numbering, and professional drafting quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, dark, uniform characters; examples (e.g., Example 15) show acceptable line weights and lettering. Prefer numerals for reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading (37 CFR 1.84(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading for opaque surfaces may be acceptable using spaced lines or stippling as appropriate; hatching technique for sectional views is defined under (h)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stippling for certain opaque surfaces; spaced lines for others. Distinguish shading from conventional hatching used to indicate proper materials (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols (37 CFR 1.84(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conventional symbols in drawings (e.g., electrical symbols). Appendix 3 discusses and shows conventional symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conventional symbol usage; see Appendix 3 for symbol list and Appendix examples showing symbol application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends — minimal wording (37 CFR 1.84(o))
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive legends should be as few words as possible to identify parts or features; computer screen images are not subject to the 'as few words as possible' requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep legends concise; examples show acceptable legends. Computer screen images may include more descriptive text where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, letters, and reference characters (37 CFR 1.84(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numbers, letters) must be clear and used to identify parts; preferably use numerals for parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match reference characters consistently between drawings and the specification; see examples illustrating acceptable reference character placement and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines (37 CFR 1.84(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are used to match reference characters to structure of the invention; they must be drawn clearly to avoid ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure lead lines do not touch or confuse adjacent features; examples demonstrate acceptable lead line usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows (37 CFR 1.84(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows indicate direction of sight, direction of motion, or may indicate a structural area. Different arrow styles or annotations may convey different meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arrows consistently; examples show arrows indicating rotation, motion, or viewing direction. Distinguish arrows that indicate areas from those indicating motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or Mask Work Notice (37 CFR 1.84(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may include a copyright or mask work notice in an acceptable form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example drawings illustrate permitted placement and appearance of copyright notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets (37 CFR 1.84(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct numbering of drawing sheets is required; all drawing sheets in an application must be the same size and properly numbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Office's numbering conventions and examples (see Example 24). Numbering must be clear and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views (37 CFR 1.84(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each view must be numbered properly (FIG. 1, FIG. 2, etc.), and numbering of subdivided views (FIG. 6A, 6B) has guidance regarding brief description consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numbering matches the specification; see Example 25 and guidance on referring to subdivided views in the brief description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings (37 CFR 1.84(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Security markings on drawings are addressed in the rules (paragraph listed under TOC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Office instructions regarding any permitted/required security markings; consult the Guide and CFR text for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and drawing changes (37 CFR 1.85 and 1.121 references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of informalities requires filing new corrected drawings; changes other than informalities normally require examiner approval and proposed changes (highlighted red-ink sketches) must be approved before allowance. Timing rules and consequences are strict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objections noted by draftsperson, Form PTO-948 is used. Corrected drawings required in a Notice of Allowability must be filed within the three-month shortened statutory period (no extensions). After allowance, Office of Patent Publication may require corrected drawings to be submitted within two months. Failure to timely comply can result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holes (37 CFR 1.84(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: Office has rules regarding holes in drawing sheets (listed as a paragraph in 37 CFR 1.84).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Office guidance on hole placement/punching so as not to interfere with margins or scanning; consult the full paragraph in the Guide/CFR for exact prohibition/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawings and special categories (37 CFR 1.84(y) and comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of drawings include black ink, color, photographs, computer screen images, chemical/mathematical figures, waveforms, program listings (limited), nucleotide/amino acid sequences (subject to separate sequence rules), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific subparagraph guidance for each type; check MPEP/PCT guidance for international/national stage specifics (appendices discuss PCT Article 7/Rule 11 and MPEP 1893.03(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of drawings — OIPE and Office Draftsperson review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility and plant drawings should be publication-ready at filing. OIPE will review drawings at filing for publication-ready quality and enter them into an electronic database for pre-grant publication; Office draftsperson reviews drawings only when the examiner seeks assistance and may complete Form PTO-948 to indicate deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings are publication-ready at filing to avoid later correction requirements. If a draftsperson issues a PTO-948, it will be mailed with examiner's next Office action. See MPEP §507 and Guide 'Processing of Drawings' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of drawing deficiencies and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings have deficiencies, examiner will note in Office action or include a Draftsperson's Notice; applicant must supply corrected/replacement drawings or submit proposed corrections pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). Examiner will approve or disapprove proposed red-ink changes; disapproval requires filing corrected drawings to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant submits an argument that a drawing requirement was improper, examiner will respond and, if not persuaded, require corrected drawings. Requests to hold requirement in abeyance are not responsive. RCEs filed without a bona fide reply that addresses drawing requirements may be held improper and application abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and deadlines for drawing corrections at allowance and after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Notice of Allowability requires corrected or new drawings, applicant must submit required drawings within three months of the mail date of the Notice of Allowability (no extensions). After allowance, if Office of Patent Publication finds drawings unacceptable for scanning/publication, applicant must submit corrected drawings within two months (no extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely submit required drawings will result in abandonment. Post-allowance voluntary new drawings may or may not be captured for publication depending on processing expediency and accompanying amendments to specification descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission by facsimile with issue fee (procedural allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO waived prohibition against submission of drawings by facsimile transmission with the issue fee; drawings may be faxed with payment of the issue fee, but applicants should consider reproducibility concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fax drawings to the specified number with the issue fee; if reproduction is unacceptable, Office will request resubmission by mail. Quality may be affected by faxing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO-948 — Notice of Draftsperson's Patent Drawing Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO-948 is used by Office draftspersons to indicate disapproval of submitted drawings and identify specific informalities in accordance with paragraphs of 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed PTO-948 is held for mailing with the next Office action. The boxed section reflects the sequence of CFR 1.84 paragraphs for indicating drafting errors; applicants must address items listed on the form in their corrections or proposals.
